en: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When a morsel of one of you falls, let him pick it up, wipe away any harm from it, and eat it, and not leave it for Satan; and let him not wipe his hand with a handkerchief until he licks his fingers, for indeed he does not know in which part of his food the blessing lies."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded the licking of fingers and the dish, and said: "Indeed, you do not know in which part of it the blessing lies."

And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sa'd, that both of them—or one of them—narrated to him from his father, Ka'b ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a similar narration.

And Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sa'd, that Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik—or Abdallah ibn Ka'b—informed him from his father, Ka'b, that he narrated to them that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to eat with three fingers, and when he finished, he would lick them.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sa'd, from the son of Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to eat with three fingers and would lick his hand before wiping it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us—they said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from the son of Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, who said: I saw the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) licking his three fingers from food. Ibn Hatim did not mention "the three". And Ibn Abi Shaybah said in his narration: "from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ka'b, from his father."

Harun ibn Abdillah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us (H); and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abu Asim informed me, both from Ibn Jurayj (H); and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is his—: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, who said: I heard Ata' saying: I heard Ibn Abbas saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you eats food, let him not wipe his hand until he licks it or has it licked."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr an-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—Ishaq said "informed us" and the others said "narrated to us"—: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you eats food, let him not wipe his hand until he licks it or has it licked."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim informed us (H); and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated it to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn Abd ar-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us, both from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a similar narration, but neither of them said "so he placed it firmly in his hand"; rather, in the narration of Ya'qub he said: "so he gave it to him."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, in what was read to him, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd as-Sa'idi: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was brought a drink and drank from it, while to his right was a boy and to his left were elders. So he said to the boy: "Do you permit me to give to these?" The boy said: "No, by Allah, I will not give preference to anyone over my share from you." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) placed it firmly in his hand.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us—they said: Isma'il—and he is Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from Abdallah ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ma'mar ibn Hazm Abu Tuwalah al-Ansari, that he heard Anas ibn Malik (H); and Abdallah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us—and the wording is his—: Sulayman—meaning Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from Abdallah ibn Abd ar-Rahman, that he heard Anas ibn Malik narrating; he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to us in our home and asked for a drink. So we milked a ewe for him, then I mixed it with water from this well of mine. He said: Then I gave it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) drank, while Abu Bakr was to his left, Umar was facing him, and a Bedouin was to his right. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) finished his drink, Umar said: "This is Abu Bakr, O Messenger of Allah," pointing him out to him. But the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gave it to the Bedouin and passed over Abu Bakr and Umar, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Those on the right, those on the right, those on the right." Anas said: "So it is a Sunnah, so it is a Sunnah, so it is a Sunnah."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr an-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived in Medina when I was ten years old, and he passed away when I was twenty years old. My mothers used to urge me to serve him. He entered upon us in our home, so we milked a domestic sheep for him and mixed it with water from a well in the house. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) drank, and Umar said to him—while Abu Bakr was to his left—: "O Messenger of Allah, give it to Abu Bakr." But he gave it to a Bedouin to his right, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The right, then the right."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was brought milk that had been mixed with water, while to his right was a Bedouin and to his left was Abu Bakr. He drank, then gave it to the Bedouin and said: "The right, then the right."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us—both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham ad-Dastawa'i, from Abu Isam, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a similar narration, and he said: "in the vessel."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id informed us (H); and Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Abu Isam, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to breathe three times while drinking and would say: "It is more quenching, more wholesome, and easier to digest." Anas said: "So I breathe three times while drinking."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Azrah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, from Thumamah ibn Abdillah ibn Anas, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to breathe three times in the vessel.

And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us (H); and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, both from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration, and in the hadith of both of them: "So I brought him a bucket."

And Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Asim, who heard ash-Sha'bi, who heard Ibn Abbas say: I gave the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) a drink from Zamzam and he drank while standing, and he had asked for a drink while he was by the House.

And Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us: Asim al-Ahwal informed us (H); and Ya'qub ad-Dawraqi and Isma'il ibn Salim narrated to me—Isma'il said "informed us" and Ya'qub said "narrated to us"—: Hushaym narrated to us: Asim al-Ahwal and Mughirah narrated to us, from ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) drank from Zamzam while standing.

And Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) drank from Zamzam from a bucket of it while standing.

And Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Asim, from ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I gave the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) a drink from Zamzam and he drank while standing.

Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ala' narrated to me: Marwan—meaning al-Fazari—narrated to us: Umar ibn Hamzah narrated to us: Abu Ghatafan al-Murri informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should drink while standing; and whoever forgets, let him vomit."

And Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's and Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Isa al-Uswari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade drinking while standing.

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Isa al-Uswari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reprimanded against drinking while standing.

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us—both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a similar narration, and he did not mention the statement of Qatadah.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): that he forbade that a man should drink while standing. Qatadah said: We said, "What about eating?" He said: "That is worse or more vile."
Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reprimanded against drinking while standing.

And Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us: Abd ar-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, a similar narration, except that he said: "And bending them back (ikhtinathuha) means turning its mouth inside out and then drinking from it."

And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade bending water skins back—that they should be drunk from directly at their mouths.

And Amr an-Naqid narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade bending water skins back.
